newsitem.title: GERMANY: German private station wins DreamWorks rights.
newsitem.headline: German private station wins DreamWorks rights.

text.p: German television company ProSieben Media AG said Wednesday it signed a deal with Hollywood studio DreamWorks for the rights to 86 films and several television series.
ProSieben said it had signed an agreement with DreamWorks, owned by Steven Spielberg, former Disney chief executive Jeffrey Katzenberg and producer David Geffen.
"With this contract, ProSieben has secured the rights to the productions of one of the most promising and creative U.S. studios," said ProSieben Media AG Chairman Georg Kofler.

Kofler said the deal would take effect in 1999 and include all the Spielberg films made after "The Lost World," his sequel to the blockbuster "Jurassic Park," and upcoming animated movies produced by Katzenberg.
ProSieben Media AG plans to sell stock to the public in July.
